headline: Oct 2016 is only partly covered by this data: 324 orders and R$44,507 revenue, against about 5,152 orders and R$701,182 in a typical month.

definitions: Partial month: fewer than 500 orders in the data
Typical month: the median month of the analysis window
Revenue: item prices of orders that are not canceled or unavailable
assumptions: Answered from the data's coverage, without a model call

evidence.sql: SELECT dc.month, dc.orders_count AS orders, dc.is_partial, dc.in_analysis_window, COUNT(o.order_id) FILTER(WHERE o.is_delivered) AS delivered_orders, ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(o.items_revenue) FILTER(WHERE o.is_sale), 0), 2) AS revenue FROM data_coverage AS dc LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.purchase_month = dc.month GROUP BY dc.month, dc.orders_count, dc.is_partial, dc.in_analysis_window ORDER BY dc.month LIMIT 501

notes: The orders run from Sep 2016 to Oct 2018, but only Jan 2017 to Aug 2018 has steady volume; the months before and after it have very few orders.
So a low figure here reflects how much of the period the data covers, not how the business performed.
caveats: The dataset does not say why these months are sparse.
